column3: The Hebrew says planted them without explicitly naming our fathers; BSB supplies that referent.
The Hebrew commands ordaining Jacob’s salvations; BSB describes God as the One who ordains victories.
The Hebrew describes goring the foes; BSB says repel.
The Hebrew presents saving and putting to shame as accomplished; BSB uses present-tense clauses.
The Hebrew does not separately express no longer; BSB adds it.
The Hebrew says the haters plundered for themselves without an explicit us object; BSB says plundered us.
The Hebrew names a shaking of the head; BSB says laughingstock.
The Hebrew says the shame of his face covered him; BSB says shame covered his face.
The Hebrew separately names an enemy and an avenger; BSB describes an enemy bent on revenge.
The Hebrew has a singular heart; BSB has hearts.
The Hebrew says we are killed; BSB says we face death.
The Hebrew has our belly in the singular; BSB has our bodies in the plural.
